stories.headline: OpenAI Proposes Robot Taxes, Public Wealth Fund in 'Industrial Policy for the Intelligence Age'

key_facts.fact: OpenAI published a 13-page policy document titled 'Industrial Policy for the Intelligence Age: Ideas to Keep People First' on April 6, presented as a starting point for debate.
The plan proposes a nationally managed public wealth fund seeded by AI companies, modeled after Alaska's Permanent Fund oil dividend, to give every American a stake in AI-driven growth.
OpenAI proposes taxing businesses that replace human workers with automated systems to compensate for reduced payroll tax revenue funding Social Security, Medicaid, and food assistance.

The document proposes auto-triggering safety nets: benefits like unemployment payments and wage insurance increase automatically when AI-driven job displacement hits preset thresholds, then phase out when conditions improve.
OpenAI proposes pilot programs testing 32-hour workweeks at full pay, framed as an 'efficiency dividend' from AI productivity gains.
Altman warns cyberattacks are 'totally possible' within one year and bioweapon creation is 'no longer theoretical,' describing them as the most immediate AI threats.
Altman told Axios that AI superintelligence is so close and disruptive that America needs a new social contract on the scale of the Progressive Era and the New Deal during the Great Depression.

stories.headline: OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar Excluded From Key Meetings as IPO Timeline Clash With Altman Widens

key_facts.fact: Sam Altman excluded CFO Sarah Friar from a major investor meeting regarding server procurement and other key financial discussions.
Friar began reporting to Fidji Simo, former Instacart CEO who oversees OpenAI's applications business, instead of directly to CEO Altman — a departure from typical CFO reporting lines.
Altman has committed OpenAI to spend $600 billion over five years on computing infrastructure and privately said he wants to go public as soon as Q4 2026.
Friar has privately said OpenAI may not be ready for a 2026 IPO, citing procedural readiness, compliance maturity, and financial risks from aggressive spending.
OpenAI anticipates spending $121 billion on computing power for AI research in 2028, with expected losses of $85 billion that year even after nearly doubling sales.
Both executives released a joint statement claiming alignment on compute strategy, stating they have 'both been directly involved in every consequential compute decision.'

stories.headline: WSJ: OpenAI and Anthropic Inference Costs Exceed Half of Revenue, Profitability Paths Diverge

key_facts.fact: Both OpenAI and Anthropic have projected profitability to investors with and without training costs, with inference costs exceeding half of total revenue for both companies.
Anthropic experienced inference costs 23% higher than internally anticipated, pushing gross margins to approximately 40%. OpenAI's projected gross margin is 46% in 2025.
Anthropic annualized revenue reached $19 billion by early 2026, closing the gap with OpenAI's $25 billion — a difference of just $6 billion.
Anthropic projects cash flow positive by 2028, while OpenAI targets 2030 — a 3-4 year divergence. OpenAI projects $21.2 billion in cash burn for 2029.
Anthropic has a $21 billion Google TPU purchase commitment, while OpenAI has 'taped out' a proprietary inference chip to reduce reliance on third-party hardware.
Anthropic derives 86% of revenue from API sales with ~9 customers spending $100M+ annually, while OpenAI gets 40% from business customers (~$5.2 billion).

stories.headline: New Yorker Publishes Major Altman Investigation With 100+ Interviews and Internal Documents

key_facts.fact: The New Yorker published a feature titled 'Sam Altman May Control Our Future. Can He Be Trusted?' for its April 13 issue, based on interviews with Altman and over 100 other people.
The article draws on 'closely guarded documents' that shed light on persistent doubts about the head of OpenAI, including allegations of persistent lying.
Interviewees are sharply divided: some defend Altman while others describe him as a sociopath.

The piece coincides with Karen Hao's book 'Empire of AI: Dreams and Nightmares in Sam Altman's OpenAI' (Penguin Press), which argues that OpenAI's unique combination of billionaire origins, ideology, and Altman's singular drive created conditions for its vision to take over.

stories.headline: Tufts Neuro-Symbolic AI Achieves 95% Accuracy With 100x Less Energy Than Standard Models

key_facts.fact: Researchers at Tufts University led by Matthias Scheutz developed a neuro-symbolic visual-language-action (VLA) system that combines neural networks with symbolic reasoning, achieving up to 100x energy reduction.

The neuro-symbolic VLA achieved a 95% success rate on the Tower of Hanoi puzzle, compared with just 34% for standard systems, and 78% on unfamiliar complex variants where traditional models scored 0%.
Training required only 1% of the energy of standard VLA systems (34 minutes vs. 36+ hours), and operational energy consumption was just 5% of conventional approaches.
The approach focuses on robotics VLA models that extend LLM capabilities by incorporating vision and physical movement, unlike chatbot-style LLMs like ChatGPT.
The work will be presented at the International Conference of Robotics and Automation (ICRA) in Vienna in May 2026.

stories.headline: Goldman Sachs Forecasts 49% Semiconductor Revenue Growth, AI Hardware Reaching $700B by Q4 2026

key_facts.fact: Goldman Sachs projects global semiconductor revenue to grow 49% from current levels by end of 2026, driven by AI-linked hardware and infrastructure demand.
AI-related hardware revenues could rise to over $700 billion in Q4 2026, according to the report.
AI-related investment in the US national accounts now stands at $325 billion (1.1% of GDP) above its 2022 level, reflecting sustained compute and server spending.
The surge is underpinned by sustained spending on data centers, servers, and advanced computing systems across the AI industry.

stories.headline: Japan Targets 30% Global Physical AI Market by 2040, Budgets $2.5B for AI and Robotics

key_facts.fact: Japan's Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) announced it aims to capture 30% of the global physical AI market by 2040, building on Japan's existing 70% share of global industrial robotics.

Tokyo budgeted 387.3 billion yen specifically for domestic AI foundation models, data infrastructure, and physical AI, within a broader 1.23 trillion yen package for AI and semiconductor development in fiscal year 2026.
Japan projects a shortage of 570,000 care workers by 2040, with nursing positions drawing only 1 applicant per 4.25 openings, driving the urgency of physical AI adoption.
FANUC announced a collaboration with NVIDIA to advance physical AI, enabling robots to interpret voice commands and automatically generate Python code without specialized programming skills.
Japan's population declined for a 14th straight year, with working-age adults at just 59.6% of the total, a share projected to shrink by nearly 15 million over the next 20 years.

Salesforce Ventures noted 'The driver has shifted from simple efficiency to industrial survival,' as Japan faces a physical supply constraint where essential services cannot be sustained due to lack of labor.

stories.headline: Spain's Xoople Raises $130M Series B to Build Satellite Constellation for AI Training Data

key_facts.fact: Xoople closed a $130 million Series B led by Nazca Capital, bringing total funding to $225 million, with the company reportedly in unicorn territory in terms of valuation.
Other investors include MCH Private Equity, CDTI (a Spanish government-backed tech development fund), Buenavista Equity Partners, and Endeavor Catalyst.
Xoople announced a deal with L3Harris Technologies to build sensors for its spacecraft, designed to collect data 'two orders of magnitude better than existing monitoring systems.'
Use cases include government agencies tracking transportation and natural disaster damage, agribusiness monitoring crop health, and firms tracking infrastructure projects and supply chains.

stories.headline: Medvi Controversy Exposes AI-Powered Healthcare Fraud: Fake Doctors, Deepfakes, FDA Warning

key_facts.fact: The New York Times profiled Medvi on April 2 as a two-employee company projecting $1.8 billion in 2026 revenue, presenting it as proof of Sam Altman's prediction that AI could enable billion-dollar one-person companies.
Gary Marcus published a viral rebuttal on April 5, calling Medvi 'a cautionary tale' about AI misuse rather than a success story, triggering widespread criticism of the NYT profile.

The FDA sent Medvi warning letter #721455 on February 20, 2026, for misbranding violations including falsely implying the company compounded semaglutide and tirzepatide and suggesting FDA approval of compounded products.
Founder Matthew Gallagher created 800+ Facebook pages posing as individual doctors with fabricated medical titles, with over 5,000 active Medvi-related ads running on Meta's platform.
Medvi used AI-generated deepfake before-and-after photos in its marketing, and a January 2026 data breach exposed records of approximately 1.6 million patients.

stories.headline: Samsung Orders ~20 EUV Machines From ASML in 10+ Trillion Won Deal for P5 Fab

key_facts.fact: Samsung Electronics ordered approximately 20 EUV lithography machines from ASML worth over 10 trillion won ($7.4 billion) for its Pyeongtaek P5 fab.
Including DUV tools from ASML and Canon, the total lithography equipment order reaches roughly 70 units for the P5 facility.
The machines will boost production of sixth-generation 1c DRAM and HBM4 memory chips, with Samsung supplying chips to Nvidia for the Rubin GPU platform.
Samsung currently operates about 40 EUV machines, roughly twice SK hynix's fleet. SK hynix recently signed its own 12 trillion won ASML deal for ~20 EUV machines.
P5 Phase 1 cleanroom completion is expected in Q1 2027, with equipment delivery and installation beginning in Q2 2027.

stories.headline: Japan Accelerates Physical AI Deployment as Labor Shortage Projected to Hit 11 Million by 2040

key_facts.fact: Japan's METI announced it aims to capture 30% of the global physical AI market by 2040, with a budget of ¥387.3 billion for AI foundation models, data infrastructure, and physical AI within a broader ¥1.23 trillion AI and semiconductor package.

Japan has 450,500 industrial robots operating in its factories, and Japanese manufacturers control approximately 70% of the global industrial robotics market, including five of the world's ten largest firms (FANUC, Yaskawa, Kawasaki, Nachi-Fujikoshi).
Mujin has deployed AI-powered robotic arms across more than 100 warehouse sites, with throughput equivalent to three to four human workers per station.
Shimizu Corporation's Robo-Welder has demonstrated a roughly 70% reduction in required human welding hours on active construction sites.
Japan projects a shortage of 11 million workers by 2040 and 570,000 care workers, with nursing positions drawing only 1 applicant per 4.25 openings.
Japan's physical AI market was valued at approximately $307 million in 2025 and is projected to reach $6.76 billion by 2035.

stories.headline: China Tightens Drone Rules With Mandatory Registration and Real-Time Tracking by May 1

key_facts.fact: Two national drone standards take effect May 1, 2026, requiring real-name registration for all civil drones and mandating that unactivated or deactivated drones be technically incapable of flight.
Drones weighing 250 grams or more require mandatory safety management and real-time location reporting, with micro drones capped at 50 meters altitude and light drones (under 4kg) at 120 meters.
Professional drone pilots reported a 'cliff-like drop in demand' after the regulations were finalized, with some pilots facing fines or confiscation for incomplete registration.
By end of 2024, China had approximately 273,000 licensed drone pilots versus 2.17 million registered drones, indicating most consumer drones were operated by unlicensed users.
Smaller drone manufacturers face cost barriers from new remote identification and registration lock requirements, while larger firms like DJI are better positioned to adapt.

stories.headline: California's Largest Proposed Data Center Faces Opposition in Imperial County

key_facts.fact: A developer plans a nearly 1 million square foot, 330MW data center on 75 acres near Aten Road and Clark Road in Imperial County, adjacent to residential neighborhoods and less than a mile from schools.

Imperial city officials filed a 231-page court complaint citing concerns about noise, hazardous emissions, fires, explosions, and toxins, saying they were not adequately consulted and environmental review was insufficient.
Residents are gathering signatures for a November 2026 ballot initiative called the 'Imperial County Data Center Prohibition Act' that would block all data centers in the county.

The developer's claims that the facility would rely on renewable energy and recycled water have been disputed, and California's Little Hoover Commission noted it is 'unclear whether such commitments would be legally binding.'
The Imperial County Board of Supervisors is scheduled to discuss the critical lot merger vote on April 7, which would determine whether construction can proceed.

stories.headline: SpaceX Scrubs Starlink Launch Seconds Before Ignition at Vandenberg Due to Winds

key_facts.fact: SpaceX halted the Starlink 17-35 launch seconds before ignition at Vandenberg Space Force Base on April 6 due to upper-level winds.
The mission was carrying 25 Starlink V2 Mini satellites destined for low Earth orbit, with a rescheduled launch window of 4:03-8:03 PM PT on April 6.
The Falcon 9 booster assigned to the mission was making its first flight, with a planned autonomous landing on the drone ship 'Of Course I Still Love You' in the Pacific Ocean.

stories.headline: Artemis II Completes Trajectory Correction on Flight Day 5, Crew Set for Monday Flyby

key_facts.fact: The Artemis II crew completed an outbound correction burn at 11:03 PM EDT on April 5, lasting 17.5 seconds, to refine Orion's trajectory toward the Moon.
The crew tested the Orion Crew Survival System (OCSS) suit, performing pressurization checks, leak tests, seat entry simulations, and mobility assessments in preparation for the flyby.

Orion's closest lunar approach will be at 7:02 PM EDT April 6 at 4,070 miles above the surface, with maximum distance from Earth of 252,760 miles at 7:07 PM — surpassing Apollo 13's 1970 record of 248,655 miles.

The crew will experience approximately 40 minutes of communications blackout as Orion passes behind the far side of the Moon starting at 6:44 PM EDT, with 'Earthrise' and signal reacquisition at 7:25 PM.
The crew reviewed 30 final lunar surface targets for observation and photography during the flyby, which is scheduled for 2:45-9:40 PM EDT on April 6.

stories.headline: Egypt, Pakistan, and Turkey Submit 45-Day Ceasefire Proposal to Iran and US

key_facts.fact: Egyptian, Pakistani, and Turkish mediators sent Iran and the US a proposal calling for a 45-day ceasefire and reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, submitted late Sunday to Iranian FM Abbas Araghchi and US envoy Steve Witkoff.
The framework, drafted by Pakistan and tentatively dubbed the 'Islamabad Agreement,' envisions a 15- to 20-day window to finalize a broader regional settlement after an immediate ceasefire.
The plan includes Iranian commitments to abandon pursuit of nuclear weapons in exchange for sanctions relief and the release of frozen assets, with Pakistan serving as the sole communication channel.

Iran rejected the idea of reopening the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for a temporary ceasefire, with a senior official telling Reuters that Tehran views Washington as lacking readiness for a permanent ceasefire.
Neither Iran nor the US had formally responded to the proposal as of Sunday night. Pakistani officials said ceasefire efforts were 'at an advanced stage' but faced 'several spoilers and detractors.'

stories.headline: Israel Strikes Iran's South Pars Petrochemical Complex, Kills Two IRGC Commanders

key_facts.fact: Israel struck a petrochemical plant at Iran's South Pars natural gas field on Monday April 6, which Israel's defense minister described as 'a powerful strike on the largest petrochemical facility in Iran, located in Asaluyeh.'
The strike killed Maj. Gen. Majid Khademi, head of intelligence for Iran's Revolutionary Guard, and Asghar Bakeri, leader of the Revolutionary Guard's undercover unit in the Quds Force.
Israel's defense minister said the facility was 'responsible for about 50% of the country's petrochemical production' and the strike aimed at eliminating a major revenue source for Iran.
Israel's defense minister vowed to continue targeting top-ranking Iranian officials, saying 'Iran's leaders live with a sense of being targeted. We will continue to hunt them down one by one.'
The strike came just as mediators floated a new 45-day ceasefire proposal, casting doubt on its viability. Explosions in Tehran and low-flying jets were heard for hours afterward.

stories.headline: Trump Threatens to Destroy Iran's Power Plants and Bridges by Tuesday

key_facts.fact: Trump posted on social media: 'Tuesday will be Power Plant Day, and Bridge Day, all wrapped up in one, in Iran. There will be nothing like it!!!' followed by 'Open the F****** Strait, you crazy b******, or you'll be living in Hell.'
Trump set the deadline for 8 p.m. Eastern Time on Tuesday (0100 GMT Wednesday), telling the Wall Street Journal the US will destroy 'every power plant' in Iran if the Strait of Hormuz isn't reopened.
Iran dismissed the threats as desperation. Deputy communications officer Seyyed Mehdi Tabatabaei said the US had 'resorted to obscenities and nonsense out of sheer desperation and anger.'
Trump has issued similar ultimatums before that he extended when mediators claimed progress, making it unclear whether he will follow through on this threat.

stories.headline: Iran Exempts Iraq from Hormuz Restrictions; First Major Crude Tanker Transits Strait

key_facts.fact: Iran's military declared Iraq exempt from Strait of Hormuz restrictions, saying limitations would only apply to 'enemy countries' and 'Brotherly Iraq is exempt from any restrictions we have imposed on the Strait of Hormuz.'
The Ocean Thunder, an Iraqi-flagged tanker loaded with roughly 1 million barrels of Basrah Heavy crude, successfully transited the Strait on April 5, tracked passing close to the Iranian coastline.
Data from LSEG and Kpler confirmed the tanker is en route to Pengerang, Malaysia, for a Petronas-chartered delivery expected in mid-April.
Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz is still down more than 90% from pre-war levels, with 53 transits last week—the most since the war began—up from 36 the previous week.
Iraq is the world's sixth-largest oil producer and second-largest in OPEC, accounting for about 4% of global supply, with oil revenues making up around 90% of its state budget.

stories.headline: Iranian Drone Strikes Damage Kuwait Power Plants and Knock Desalination Offline

key_facts.fact: Iranian drones and missiles struck multiple sites in Kuwait on April 5, including the Shuwaikh Oil Sector Complex and two power and water desalination plants, causing significant material damage.

Kuwait's Ministry of Electricity reported the strikes took a water desalination station out of service and shut two electricity-generating units. Emergency plans were activated to ensure service continuity.
The Shuwaikh complex was evacuated after fires were reported at key oil and government facilities. No casualties were confirmed by Kuwaiti authorities.

Bahrain also experienced drone attacks causing fires at national oil company storage and a state-run petrochemical plant. The UAE responded to fires at a Ruwais petrochemical plant from intercepted debris, halting operations.

The overall conflict death toll stands at over 1,900 killed in Iran, 1,400+ in Lebanon with over 1 million displaced, 20+ across Gulf states and the West Bank, 23 in Israel, and 13 US service members.

stories.headline: Oil Prices Swing Between $108-$114 on Trump Threats and Ceasefire Hopes

key_facts.fact: Brent crude rose 1.4% to $110.60 and US WTI crude rose 1.8% to $113.60 on Sunday after Trump threatened to strike Iranian energy facilities if the Strait of Hormuz is not reopened.
Oil then switched from gains to losses as traders weighed a reported push for a ceasefire against the fresh Trump ultimatum. WTI dropped about 1% to $110.45 and Brent was little changed at $108.76.
By early Asia trading on April 6, Brent crude was up 0.7% at $109.80 while US crude hovered near $111.62, reflecting ongoing uncertainty.
Stock futures dropped alongside the oil price swings, with Fortune reporting fuel shortages mounting as Hormuz remains effectively closed to most shipping.

stories.headline: Artemis II Completes Course Correction, Crew Set for Historic Lunar Flyby

key_facts.fact: The Orion spacecraft completed a 17.5-second outbound correction burn at 11:03 p.m. EDT on April 5 to refine its trajectory toward the Moon.

The crew entered the Moon's sphere of influence at 12:41 a.m. EDT on April 6. The flyby window runs from 2:45-9:40 PM EDT April 6, with closest approach at 4,070 miles from the lunar surface at 7:02 p.m.
At 1:56 p.m. EDT April 6, the crew will surpass Apollo 13's record for humans' farthest distance from Earth, reaching a maximum distance of 252,757 miles—4,105 miles farther than Apollo 13.

All four crew members—Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen—completed testing of the Orion Crew Survival System suits including pressurization, leak checks, and simulated seat entry.
NASA scientists identified about 35 geological features for the crew to observe during the flyby. The crew will work in pairs to photograph sites and describe them in real time to Mission Control.
Orion will pass behind the Moon at 6:44 p.m. EDT, losing communications for approximately 40 minutes. 'Earthrise' and signal reacquisition are expected at 7:25 p.m.

stories.headline: Wipro Acquires Olam's IT Arm Mindsprint for $375M, Signs $1B Strategic Deal

key_facts.fact: Wipro will acquire 100% of Mindsprint, Olam Group's IT services subsidiary, in a cash deal valued at $375 million, with closing expected by June 30, 2026 pending regulatory approvals.
The 8-year strategic transformation engagement with Olam Group is expected to exceed $1 billion in contract value, with a committed spend of $800 million.

Mindsprint employs over 3,200 people across India, Singapore, the US, UK, and the Middle East, and operates proprietary platforms including Farmsprint (plantation management) and Procuresprint (AI-enabled procurement).
Olam Group is a US$50+ billion revenue food and agri-business company headquartered in Singapore with ~40,000 employees, majority owned by Temasek Holdings.
Wipro shares jumped over 3% on the news. Wipro will deliver end-to-end transformation across Olam's 'farm-to-fork' value chain using its Wipro Intelligence AI platform.

stories.headline: Drift Reveals $270M Crypto Exploit Was a Six-Month North Korean Intelligence Op

key_facts.fact: Drift Protocol, the largest decentralized perpetual futures exchange on Solana, revealed on April 5 that its $270M exploit on April 1 was a six-month intelligence operation by a North Korean state-affiliated group.

The attackers first made contact at a major crypto conference around fall 2025, posing as a quantitative trading firm. They onboarded an Ecosystem Vault, deposited over $1 million of their own capital, and held multiple working sessions with contributors.

The attacker abused Solana's 'durable nonces' feature to pre-sign transactions that remained valid for over a week, then obtained two misleading approvals from Drift's five-member Security Council multisig to seize protocol control in minutes.

Blockchain analytics firm Elliptic flagged the exploit as consistent with previous DPRK-attributed operations based on on-chain behavior, laundering methodologies, and network-level indicators. Total DPRK crypto theft in 2026 exceeds $300 million.
TRM Labs confirmed the attack represents the eighteenth DPRK-linked crypto operation tracked in 2026, making North Korea the most prolific state-sponsored crypto threat actor.

stories.headline: OpenAI Proposes Robot Taxes, Public Wealth Fund, 4-Day Workweek for AI Era

key_facts.fact: OpenAI released 'Industrial Policy for the Intelligence Age: Ideas to Keep People First,' proposing policies for a world with AI superintelligence including a public wealth fund, taxes on automated labor, and a potential four-day workweek.
The proposal calls for lawmakers and AI companies to jointly invest in a public wealth fund linked to the AI boom, with returns distributed directly to citizens.
OpenAI suggests actively measuring how AI affects wages and unemployment, and once 'these metrics exceed pre-defined thresholds,' offering workers increased unemployment benefits or job training.
The document proposes incentivizing employers to experiment with four-day workweeks as a way to let workers share in AI-driven efficiency gains, as long as output doesn't fall.
Sam Altman told Axios he feels 'urgency' about the power of coming AI models and called the proposals a 'New Deal for superintelligence' to 'wake up DC.'
